name: Primary Intestinal Lymphangiectasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Primary Intestinal Lymphangiectasia

criteria.description: Histological evidence of dilated intestinal lymphatic vessels on biopsy
Clinical and laboratory evidence of protein-losing enteropathy (hypoalbuminemia, hypogammaglobulinemia)
Presence of peripheral edema due to hypoproteinemia
Imaging evidence (e.g. lymphangiography, MRI) of intestinal lymphatic dilation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of dilated intestinal lymphatics plus clinical evidence of protein-losing enteropathy and edema
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by exclusion of secondary causes of intestinal lymphangiectasia

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to hypoalbuminemia and immunoglobulin loss

common.notes: Due to lymphatic dilation and edema
Related to protein loss and malnutrition

occasional.notes: Fat malabsorption due to lymphatic dysfunction
Due to lymph leakage and hypoalbuminemia
In pediatric patients due to malnutrition

rare.notes: Due to lymph leakage into pleural space

imaging: MRI or CT demonstrating intestinal wall thickening and lymphatic dilation
Ultrasound showing ascites or pleural effusion
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; primarily sporadic or congenital malformation
other: Endoscopic findings of white, dilated mucosal lymphatics
Histopathology confirming dilated lymphatic vessels in intestinal mucosa

distinguishingFeatures: Secondary to conditions like constrictive pericarditis, lymphoma, or infections
Reversible with treatment of primary cause
Multiple etiologies including inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease
No primary lymphatic dilation on biopsy
May have different endoscopic and histologic findings
Predominantly chylous ascites without significant intestinal lymphangiectasia

redFlags: Recurrent severe infections due to immunoglobulin loss
Development of chylous effusions (pleural or ascitic)
references: Waldmann TA, Steinfeld JL, Dutcher TF, Davidson JD, Gordon RS Jr. The role of intestinal lymphangiectasia in the pathogenesis of hypoproteinemia. J Clin Invest. 1961.
Fouquet V, et al. Primary intestinal lymphangiectasia: clinical, histological, and therapeutic aspects. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2018.
Meyer A, et al. Diagnosis and management of primary intestinal lymphangiectasia: a systematic review. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2020.
